reviewedPurpose: Cumulative pure-WLD circuit-world ABI 2 with four-argument begin, bounded retained-pixel query and no sidecar parser/session/source/save or custom color mapping. Default OFF retains vanilla per-TripWire type-445 horizontal/vertical crossing XOR. ON combines device generation dedup with WireHead-style per-pixel different-colour connected-group pair parity at each shared physical gate-wave boundary; incompatible same-colour dual-axis topology rejects ON with TCW_UNSUPPORTED without mutation. This is a restricted pixel rule, not a full WireHead topology emulator or its multi-pixel dictionary-overwrite behavior. Idle switching preserves frames, ROM/RAM, input and RNG. Physical gate-wave rules retain their prior policy; the VM now allows bounded resumable trip-end work before pixel and gate evaluation. Cold-load compilation enumerates wired/gate rows in original order, uses inline paged DSU accessors and bounds-checked tile reads without duplicate checks; every input tile record remains decoded and validated and temporary row indexes are freed after compilation. Export the four existing incremental SHA-256 functions in the WLD Web profile for bounded native hashing by the host; the existing C hash implementation is byte-identical to the frozen v3 source. Sparse READ_LAMPS queries restore existing 64-column checkpoints only at complete-column boundaries when the next requested point has a later checkpoint, preserve original point order/duplicates, and yield immediately after each restore. Compilation, source validation, viewport, write, trigger, simulation and save semantics are unchanged. Add independently implemented ordinary type-42 hanging lantern and type-93 standing lamp wire responses. Retain only connected light footprints and required unwired siblings, deduplicate each complete footprint per wire colour and TripWire, preserve style frames, and project all mutated members into queries and candidate WLD saves. Unsupported malformed or directional pre-actuated footprints fail transactionally instead of approximating source behavior. Add independent source-oracle FIFO timer encounter replay for bounded ordinary-wire multi-timer domains. Seed rectangles preserve x/y enumeration, colours red/blue/green/yellow, and down/up/right/left FIFO traversal; timer registration order precedes existing reverse mechanical ticking. Optional topology and bounded seed-order caches yield between work units and are evictable under mandatory allocation pressure. Unsupported directional multi-timer topology or unavailable ordering data rejects the affected command transactionally instead of using coordinate order. Single-timer worlds do not retain the optional ordering graph. This does not claim full Terraria wiring parity. Add an optional bounded viewport source-value cache for rectangles of at most 4096 cells. Cache entries retain original tiles and topology references; every query projects current circuit state. Warm immutable-source queries issue a host validation read without changing scan input state. Pinned entries survive active query work; cancellation, errors, close and optimization changes discard them. Owner and private VM allocation paths may reclaim unpinned entries while preserving the total memory ceiling. Public ABI and exports remain unchanged. This provenance update identifies source only; a rebuilt runtime must be recorded and verified separately. Streamed TOPOLOGY/COUNT/WRITE stage-1 compilation binds the existing input window once per uninterrupted decode batch, preserving the original 32-byte readiness rule and per-record decoder. Every return, error, host event and column-end handler restores the original TxWorld file pointer and length; original allocation and metadata aliases remain alive. No new allocation, retained cache, ABI, export, IO or source-validation shortcut is introduced. Native-host performance evidence is separate from Web and device behavior. Runtime artifacts require an actual rebuilt and verified source-manifest chain.
